decisions.quote: Like our study, Bau and Mackay found OctoPocus significantly more accurate than a crib-sheet baseline, suggesting that OctoPocus is better at training people to perform more precise gesture movements in 2D and 3D. However, Bau and Mackay also found overall trial time for OctoPocus lower than crib-sheet, while we observed no overall difference in trial time, there is a trade-off between reaction time and input time. Bau and Mackay found no difference between conditions for input time or reaction time. In addition, Bau and Mackay found a significantly higher post-test recall for OctoPocus, but this appears to be because recall for our crib-sheet condition (83%) was much better than Bau and Mackay’s (57%).
decisions.reason: While the replication confirmed Bau and Mackay's (2008) finding that OctoPocus is significantly more accurate than a crib-sheet baseline, the authors explicitly contrast their other tested findings with the original, observing no overall trial-time difference and no advantage for recall or incidental learning.
